  • status: "mismatch": those build IDs differ; restart_recommended: true and hint suggest asking the user to save work and restart, then check status and list tabs again. This is evidence of a pending browser restart, not proof of the cause of a page failure.
  • status: "unknown": restart_recommended: null and a reason; not a healthy/matching result.

Runtime metadata is sent by the extension on each connection, not read from page content or a user agent string. Installed-build inspection is currently macOS only. The bridge matches the exact reverse TCP connection of its active extension WebSocket to one PID using lsof, verifies the main executable against its bundle's Info.plist, and reads the current bundle's application.ini. mapped_bundle says current (Contents) or backup (Contents.bak); a backup path alone is not a build mismatch. It never picks a browser by name from the process list or reads a user profile. Each of at most three lsof calls has a one-second timeout, and metadata files are capped at 64 KiB. The peer is rechecked after inspection; a replaced/disconnected extension invalidates the result. The diagnostic returns no paths, PIDs, socket addresses, tokens, or raw subprocess errors.

Unknown reasons include extension_disconnected, runtime_info_unavailable (older extension or runtime metadata not yet received), unsupported_platform (installed-build inspection unavailable), connection_address_unavailable, browser_process_unavailable, ambiguous_browser_process, process_lookup_unavailable (missing helper or access denied), process_lookup_failed, process_lookup_timeout, browser_bundle_unavailable, installed_metadata_unavailable, build_id_unavailable, and connection_changed. A remote/forwarded WebSocket that cannot be tied to a local browser is also unknown, not guessed.

This is read-only: no tabs are opened, navigated, activated or closed; no settings change, extension reload, or browser restart is performed. A bridge predating this option may ignore the query: absence of browser_diagnostics is not a successful build comparison.

docs.title: GET /api/version
docs.text:
Bridge and extension version info. 

{ "bridge": "0.7.3", "api": "1", "extension_connected": true, "extension_version": "0.7.3", "extension_build": "dev", "extension": 25 }

docs.title: GET /api/page-info
docs.text:
Page metadata plus current dialog policy and recent dialog history. Never cached. Also accepts POST with { "tabId": 123 }. MCP tool: browser_page_info(tab_id=None). 

{ "url": "...", "title": "...", "readyState": "complete", "lang": "en", "width": 890, "height": 992, "forms": 0, "links": 1, "images": 0 }
readyState is the document's document.readyState; see Snapshot readiness. A page that shows a sign-in field or a CAPTCHA adds a needs_user hint.

docs.title: GET /api/page-text
docs.text:
All visible text on the page. 

{ "text": "..." }

docs.title: GET /api/tabs
docs.text:
All open browser tabs. 

{ "tabs": [{ "id": 1, "url": "...", "title": "...", "active": true, "windowId": 1, "index": 0, "owned": true, "mine": true }] }
mine: true marks the tabs the request's X-Kitsune-Owner opened. POST with { "mine": true } returns only those, the most recently opened first (see Tab owners).

docs.title: GET /api/dom
docs.text:
Accessibility tree (depth=6). POST accepts tabId, selector, ref and maxDepth, scoped as in browser_dom. 

{ "tree": { "ref": "s1e0", "tag": "body", "children": [...] }, "refs": 42 }
Sensitive fields report redacted/hasValue instead of value. A tree past the 20,000-char cap also has "truncated": true and a hint.

docs.title: GET /api/forms
docs.text:
All form fields on the page. Sensitive fields have redacted/hasValue instead of value (see Sensitive-field redaction). 

{ "fields": [{ "ref": "e0", "tag": "input", "type": "password", "name": "password", "id": "password", "placeholder": "", "redacted": true, "hasValue": true, "label": "Password", "required": false, "selector": "#password", "bounds": [...] }] }

docs.title: GET /api/screenshot
docs.text:
Captures the active page as PNG and saves to the bridge screenshot directory ($KITSUNE_HOME/screenshots, default ~/.kitsune/screenshots). 

{ "url": "...", "title": "...", "saved_to": "...", "filename": "kitsune_20260313_120000.png" }

docs.title: POST /api/screenshot, /api/element-screenshot, /api/full-page-screenshot
docs.text:
Return dataUrl and capture metadata. Set imagePreview: true for an inline preview under roughly 1 MB (large images are JPEG-encoded and downscaled in the extension). Without that flag, return full PNG data by default, or JPEG with format: "jpeg". Viewport requests accept tabId. Element requests require selector and accept tabId and scale (1–4); full-page requests accept tabId. A capture never shows the tab (tabs.captureTab). Captures retain existing canvas and scroll/segment limits and can truncate very large documents.

MCP tool browser_screenshot(selector=None, full_page=False, tab_id=None, save_to=None, data_url=False, ref=None, element=None, format="png") returns [Image, metadata] by default, giving the model actual MCP image content. save_to writes the full requested PNG/JPEG and returns metadata with saved_to instead. data_url=True returns the raw image data in metadata. Inline preview dimensions can be smaller than the original capture metadata.

docs.title: POST /api/handle-dialog
docs.text:
{ "accept": true, "prompt_text": "answer", "tabId": 123 }

MCP tool: browser_handle_dialog(accept=True, prompt_text=None, tab_id=None). Sets the tab's policy for subsequent dialogs and returns {ok, policy, dialogs}. By default, with no policy, original native alert/confirm/prompt functions run and the user's actual response is recorded. beforeunload also keeps native behavior. Only an explicitly configured policy auto-answers dialogs. Clear a policy with browser_handle_dialog(accept=None, tab_id=123) or HTTP { "accept": null, "tabId": 123 } to restore native pass-through. Accepted prompts return prompt_text if supplied, otherwise the prompt's default; dismissed prompts return null and dismissed confirms return false. With a policy set, alerts return immediately; in native mode they wait for the user. Recent history is also included in browser_page_info:

{ "policy": { "accept": true, "prompt_text": "answer" }, "dialogs": [
  { "type": "prompt", "message": "Name?", "default_value": "Guest",
    "timestamp": 1792200000000, "response": "answer", "pending": false }
] }

The page-world override records every intercepted invocation (last 100 per document). Answers are synchronous; pending: false means the user's native response or configured automatic answer was already returned, and a later tool call cannot change it. Alert responses are null (no return value). Policies persist across navigation until tab closure or extension restart, with native behavior applying until asynchronous restoration completes. Clearing a policy also removes it from the per-tab policy store. Capture starts at document_start for new documents and on connection for existing tabs. Scripts holding original references before injection, iframe dialogs (including cross-origin frames), browser-internal pages, and already-open native dialogs are outside this mechanism. Page scripts can also replace or bypass the overrides.

accept: true also disarms beforeunload using the same returnValue/preventDefault suppression as browser_close_tab(force=True), allowing navigation away. Unload events are recorded with type beforeunload. accept: false leaves native unload behavior; the extension cannot answer a native “Leave page?” prompt. Accepting temporarily clears onbeforeunload; clearing or dismissing the policy restores the saved handler if the page has not supplied a replacement. Force-closing remains available regardless of dialog policy.

docs.title: POST /api/wait-for-text
docs.text:
{ "text": "Ready", "text_gone": "Loading", "timeout": 10000, "tabId": 123 }

MCP tool: browser_wait_for(text=...) or browser_wait_for(text_gone=...). Provide at least one non-empty condition (the HTTP endpoint accepts both at once). Polls rendered top-level document text about every 100 ms, excluding hidden text; if both conditions are provided they must both hold. Matching uses case-sensitive substrings. Frames and shadow roots are not traversed. Field names from placeholder, aria-label or aria-labelledby, which snapshots show as names, are not page text and never match. Returns {ok, text, text_gone, elapsed}; timeout returns ok: false with an error. When the text of a timed-out text wait is the name of a visible element, the result also has matched_as: "accessible_name", name_matches (up to 3 {ref, role, name, source}, where source is the attribute) and a hint: act on the ref, or wait for text the page shows. A text wait met by its first read, because the text was already on the page (in a field's label, say), adds already_present: true and a hint (#402). With "new_only": true (browser_wait_for(new_only=True); the core tool's newOnly is accepted but not published), the wait counts the text's occurrences at its start and is met only once more occur. The bridge polls single reads (see browser_wait_for); a zero timeout performs one immediate check.

docs.title: POST /api/navigate
docs.text: { "url": "https://example.com", "tabId": 1, "expectTitle": "Example" } - tabId optional (defaults to active tab) - expectTitle optional — warns if title doesn't match (catches silent redirects) - User and other clients' tabs return user_tab_read_only without a prompt; the same applies to /api/back, /api/forward and reload. Explicit compatibility opt-outs are described in Protecting your tabs. - A load that does not finish in 15 s returns { "ok": false, "timedOut": true, "url": "..." }. If the tab is still about:blank / complete and the page cannot confirm a loaded destination, it also carries code: "navigation_stalled", retryable: false, and the recovery hint of new_tab_stalled (#366). A requested about: URL never gets this code.

docs.title: POST /api/back
docs.text: { "tabId": 1 } goes back in the tab's history and returns { "ok": true, "tabId": 1 } once dispatched. "pageText": true, an internal flag the core browser_navigate_back sends, waits for the page it loads and adds the page's readable snapshot when it fits 2,000 characters (see Post-action snapshots, #448). With KITSUNE_POST_ACTION_SNAPSHOT=0 the flag does nothing.

docs.title: POST /api/new-tab
docs.text:
{ "url": "https://example.com" } — url optional, defaults to about:blank. Opens an agent-owned tab in the background (it is not shown; see Shared browser). Returns { "ok": true, "tabId": 123 } immediately.

{ "url": "https://example.com", "wait": true, "timeout": 15000 } waits up to timeout ms (default 15000) for the load and returns { "ok": true, "tabId": 123, "url": "https://example.com/after-redirect", "status": "complete" }. On timeout the tab stays open and the result is { "ok": false, "timedOut": true, "tabId": 123, "url": "...", "status": "loading" }. While Zen's first-run welcome screen is open, the browser keeps reporting a loaded tab's URL as about:blank (#360); the wait then asks the page, and url is the page's own URL. With wait, "pageText": true, an internal flag the core browser_tabs action=new url=… sends, adds the loaded page's readable snapshot when it fits 2,000 characters, as a browser_navigate result has it (#448); a larger page, a timeout or KITSUNE_POST_ACTION_SNAPSHOT=0 adds nothing.

If the wait times out with the tab still about:blank / complete, and the page cannot confirm a loaded destination, the result also carries code: "new_tab_stalled", retryable: false, and a hint saying that retrying will not fix it (#366). The tab already exists: tabId is retained (the core browser_tabs returns its index and tab list instead). Do not repeat creation or navigation: the browser needs an update, a restart or another fix first. A browser left running after an on-disk update is one possible cause; check browser_status(diagnostics=true) for build mismatch evidence. Tell the user, ask them to save work and restart or update the browser (or fix it another way), and retry only after they say it is fixed. The code describes the observed blank-tab timeout, not a confirmed update mismatch. Kitsune does not restart the browser, activate the tab, or create a replacement automatically. A blank tab requested intentionally still succeeds; a tab still loading retains the ordinary timeout result.

docs.title: POST /api/switch-tab
docs.text: { "tabId": 123 } shows the tab. It switches the user's view, so send it only on the user's request; while the user is using the tab it would hide, it returns user_active.

docs.title: POST /api/close-tab
docs.text: { "tabId": 123, "force": true, "confirmToken": "…" } closes a tab this client may write; any other tab returns user_tab_read_only (see Tab permissions). With a v0.7.1 extension, a tab the agent did not open returns needs_user (user_tab) with a confirm token instead; confirmToken is that token after the user approved. force disarms beforeunload first.

docs.title: POST /api/wake-tab
docs.text:
{ "tabId": 123 } reloads a discarded tab this client may write; reads of a discarded tab of any owner wake it themselves (#449). A tab that is not discarded returns { "ok": true, "woken": false, "discarded": false } at once. Otherwise the call waits up to 15 s for the reloaded page to finish loading and answer the content script, and then returns { "ok": true, "woken": true, "ready": true }; the next command can reach the page. Two results report ready: false: - { "ok": true, "woken": true, "ready": false, "unscriptable": true, "state": { "tabId", "url", "status", "title", "httpStatus" } }: the reloaded page loaded but refuses the content script, such as a JSON or PDF viewer or an error response with an empty body. Commands fail with error_page. - { "ok": true, "woken": true, "ready": false, "timedOut": true, "state": { "tabId", "url", "status" } }: the page did not become ready within 15 s; state is the last observed state. state.reason: "no_receiver" means the last check found the reloaded page loaded and accepting the content script, but nothing answered its ping. While the page stays silent, commands fail with content_unavailable (state.reason: "no_receiver") before anything is sent.

Ready means the content script answered a ping after the load, not that an injection succeeded. Until the deadline, each check injects and pings again, so a page that starts answering late still ends the wait as ready. Each ping waits at most 1 s; the injection is one browser call whose own duration the deadline cannot cut short.

docs.title: POST /api/click
docs.text:
{ "selector": "button.submit" } — also accepts ref, position.

The click moves to the target before pressing: pointerover/mouseover, non-bubbling pointerenter/mouseenter on newly entered ancestors and the target, then pointermove/mousemove, sharing browser_hover's pointer tracking. A drag also moves to its source before pressing. The click then dispatches pointerdown, mousedown, pointerup, mouseup and click at the target's center or the given point. For a primary-button press, button: 0; buttons is 0 during approach, 1 at the press and 0 from pointerup on. click is a PointerEvent with detail: 1 and pointerType: "mouse", and it runs the element's native activation once, as el.click() does; a disabled form control gets no click. Limits: every event has isTrusted: false and grants no user activation, and no pointerout or pointerleave is sent. For pages that need trusted input, use browser_trusted_click; an unmet expect whose target is still visible says so in its hint (see Action outcomes).

"holdMs": 600 (0-10000; MCP hold_ms) holds the press for long-press controls (#351): pointerup, mouseup and click (or contextmenu/auxclick) follow that long after pointerdown and mousedown, and the result adds held_ms, the measured hold. The background times the hold, because a hidden tab's page timers fire after 1 s at the earliest; measured in a background tab, a 700 ms hold lasted 729 ms. Any other value returns holdMs must be an integer from 0 to 10000 and dispatches nothing. Add "wait": true, "timeout": 10000 to wait for the target first (see Actionability wait); the other action endpoints accept the same keys.

docs.title: POST /api/trusted-click
docs.text: { "selector": "button.submit", "focus": true } or { "coords": { "x": 640, "y": 400 }, "coordinateSpace": "viewport" } — optional tabId, title, process, restorePointer, button (left/right/middle), clickCount (1 or 2), modifiers (["Shift", "Control", "Alt", "Meta"]). OS-level click on Windows, macOS and Linux (X11); see browser_trusted_click. holdMs (0-10000) holds a single click's press. A click that does not finish within 35 s returns a timeout action error with retryable: false.

docs.title: POST /api/trusted-drag
docs.text: { "selector": "#knob", "to": "#mark", "steps": 10 } — refs work for both, plus optional tabId, first, process and focus (false leaves bringing the browser to the front to the caller). OS-level drag on macOS; see browser_trusted_drag. A drag that does not finish within 35 s returns a timeout action error.

docs.title: POST /api/type
docs.text: { "text": "hello", "selector": "input" }

docs.title: POST /api/fill
docs.text:
{ "selector": "input#email", "value": "user@example.com" } Handles shadow DOM and React/Vue state. A web-component host is filled through the first input, textarea or select in its open or closed shadow root, else in the shadow roots of hosts nested inside it, up to 8 roots deep (closed roots through Firefox's openOrClosedShadowRoot). /api/type, /api/set-editable-content and /api/form-fill use the same lookup. When /api/fill, /api/type or a /api/form-fill key cannot reach a field, the result is a not_fillable action error.

An ARIA slider or spinbutton (role=slider/spinbutton with a numeric aria-valuenow and no native field) has no value to assign, so /api/fill sets it with keys, in the page, in one request (#311): it focuses the target and presses Home or End when the value is aria-valuemin or aria-valuemax, then arrow keys toward the value (ArrowRight/ArrowLeft on a horizontal slider, ArrowUp/ArrowDown on a vertical one or a spinbutton; the other pair when the first does not move it toward the value). Keys are keydown/keyup on the target as /api/keypress dispatches them, a task apart so the page renders each step; a widget that renders only on an animation frame is not waited for, so it looks stuck. The value must be a number; values are compared up to float rounding. It stops at the value: { "ok": true, "tag": "div", "role": "slider", "value": 15, "target": 15, "min": 0, "max": 100, "keys": 35 }. A value outside aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax is a value_not_reached action error (reason: "out_of_range", keys: 0, retryable: true) before any key. When a key steps past the value, a key stops moving it, the arrow keys move it away, or 1,000 keys or 20 s run out, it is a value_not_reached with retryable: false and the same state. A native <input type=range>, also inside a role=slider wrapper, keeps the value setter.

docs.title: POST /api/scroll
docs.text: { "direction": "down", "amount": 500 } — optional container selector or ref; element is an audit-only description. Needs browse; with loadMore: true (the core browser_find's load_more scrolls, #447) core also permits it.

docs.title: POST /api/hover
docs.text:
{ "selector": "a.link" } Returns { "ok": true, "tag": "a" }, plus opened_popup when the hover opened a menu, listbox or dialog.

A selector is scrolled into view first. The hover dispatches, in this order, pointerover, pointerenter, mouseover, mouseenter, pointermove and mousemove at the target's center, as a pointer arriving there would. pointerover, mouseover and the move events go to the target and bubble, across shadow roots (composed: true). pointerenter and mouseenter do not bubble; each goes to every newly entered element from the outermost ancestor to the target, so a row that shows its controls on enter sees the hover of a child. The ancestor chain crosses shadow roots to their hosts and stays within the target's document (in a frame, the <iframe> element is not entered). An ancestor that also contains the element the previous hover pointed at counts as already entered and gets no enter events; the first hover enters every ancestor up to the root element, and so does hovering the same element again, so a retry can reveal what was hidden meanwhile. Kitsune remembers only its own hovers in this document: clicks, the real pointer and browser_trusted_click do not change it, and navigation or reinjection starts over. Pointer events carry pointerType: "mouse", pointerId: 1 and isPrimary, and every event carries view and the point.

Limits: every event has isTrusted: false, and no pointerout, pointerleave, mouseout or mouseleave is sent to the element pointed at before. CSS :hover rules follow only the real pointer, so a control that only a :hover style reveals stays hidden. For it, use browser_trusted_click with restore_pointer=False, which clicks the target with the real pointer and leaves the pointer there, on a target where a click is harmless; or ask the user to point at it.

"durationMs": 400 (0-10000; MCP duration_ms) and "steps": 5 (1-50) keep the pointer moving, for hover-intent controls that wait for several moves over some time (#351). After the hover above, which then arrives at a quarter of the target's width, steps more pointermove/mousemove pairs cross the middle half of the target from left to right at its vertical center, spread evenly over durationMs (5 steps when only durationMs is given), or a task apart without it. The result adds moves (steps + 1) and hovered_ms. As for a held click, the background times the pauses: in a background tab, a 500 ms hover with 5 steps took 579 ms. Values out of range return an error and move nothing.

docs.title: POST /api/drag
docs.text: { "from": "#card", "to": "#done" } — or ref and toRef. Returns { "ok": true, "from": "#card", "to": "#done", "via": "html5" }. It presses the source (pointerdown, mousedown) and dispatches the HTML5 drag events (dragstart … drop, dragend). They count (via: "html5") when the source is draggable, the page let dragstart through and the destination accepted the drop by cancelling dragenter, dragover or drop, as a browser requires. Otherwise the drag is replayed as a pointer drag (via: "pointer") for libraries that build drag on pointer events: ten pointermove/mousemove steps from the source's center to the destination's, so a drag threshold is crossed, each in a new task so the page can render in between; then pointerup and mouseup. Pointer events (pointerId: 1, buttons: 1, isPrimary) go to the source, where setPointerCapture routes them; the page's capture itself is not visible to Kitsune, and Firefox can throw NotFoundError from setPointerCapture for a pointer it has not seen, such as this synthetic one. mouseup lands on the destination.

docs.title: POST /api/find
docs.text: { "query": "search text" } or { "selector": "a.link" } Both query and selector are accepted (normalized to query internally). Returns { "results": [{ "ref": "r0", "tag": "a", "text": "...", "selector": "...", "bounds": [...] }] } A query that is not a matching CSS selector is split into words (filler words such as "the" or "in" are dropped). Elements are scored per word they match in their text, aria-label, placeholder, title, alt, id, name or value, or a role word ("button", "dropdown", "search bar"), with more for matching every word and for the whole query or a quoted part as a phrase. Only matching elements are returned, best first; when nothing matches, the reply is { "results": [], "hint": "..." }.

docs.title: POST /api/js
docs.text: { "code": "document.title" } Returns { "result": "..." }. Results capped at 50KB with truncation flag. Page JavaScript is not subject to password redaction.

docs.title: POST /api/highlight
docs.text: { "selector": "h1" } — draws red border overlay on element.

docs.title: POST /api/clear-highlight
docs.text: No body needed. Removes all highlights.

docs.title: POST /api/wait-for-element
docs.text: { "selector": ".loaded", "timeout": 10000, "pollInterval": 200 } Polls until element appears. Returns { "ok": true, "found": true, "ref": "r0", "elapsed": 1200 }; timeout returns ok: false, found: false with an error. The bridge polls single reads (see browser_wait_for); a zero timeout performs one immediate check.

docs.title: POST /api/wait-for-result
docs.text: { "code": "document.querySelector('.data')?.textContent", "timeout": 15000, "pollInterval": 500 } Polls JS expression until non-empty. Returns { "ok": true, "result": "...", "elapsed": 2000, "polls": 4 }

docs.title: POST /api/page-text-by-tab-id
docs.text: { "tabId": 123 } — get text from a specific tab (not just active).

docs.title: POST /api/batch
docs.text:
Execute multiple commands sequentially or in parallel. 

{
  "commands": [
    { "action": "navigate", "url": "https://example.com" },
    { "action": "sleep", "ms": 2000 },
    { "action": "pageText" }
  ],
  "stopOnWarning": false,
  "tabId": 12
}
tabId (optional) is the tab for commands that name none; see Container progress for how steps pick their tab.

Parallel sequences (commands within each sequence run sequentially, sequences run concurrently): 

{
  "commands": [{
    "action": "parallel",
    "sequences": [
      [{ "action": "navigate", "tabId": 1, "url": "https://a.com" }, { "action": "pageText", "tabId": 1 }],
      [{ "action": "navigate", "tabId": 2, "url": "https://b.com" }, { "action": "pageText", "tabId": 2 }]
    ]
  }]
}
Note: every command that acts on a tab inside parallel sequences must have an explicit tabId, and two sequences may not write the same tab (see Container progress).

Returns { "results": [...], "progress": [...], "status": "ok", "summary": "..." }; progress, status and summary are described in Container progress. When newTab commands, nested ones included, opened tabs that a later closeTab command did not close, newTabs lists their ids, oldest first; the MCP server makes the last one its current tab (No current tab).

A response whose status is not ok adds call and resume_token for POST /api/resume.

Batch actions: navigate, newTab, closeTab, switchTab, click, type, fill, scroll, hover, find, js, pageInfo, pageText, pageTextByTabId, tabs, forms, dom, highlight, screenshot, waitForElement, waitForResult, sleep, parallel, media (see Media).

docs.title: POST /api/resume
docs.text:
Continue a batch, parallel or workflow call that did not finish ok (browser_resume). A direct call's checkpoint is in the MCP server, so this route answers checkpoint_not_found for its call. 

{ "call": 42, "resume_token": "x3J...", "observed": { "1": "not_applied", "0.1.2": "applied" } }
Returns the original call's response shape; see Checkpoint and resume.

docs.title: POST /api/ask-user
docs.text:
The needs_user stop of browser_ask_user (#376); nothing reaches the page. tabId is optional. 

{ "reason": "sign_in", "message": "Sign in to your shop account, please.", "tabId": 12 }
Returns needs_user with state.reason: "agent_request", state.detail (the reason), state.message, the tab's tabId, url and title, state.evidence when the tab shows that hint, and call; see browser_ask_user. Asking the user is the MCP server's.

docs.title: POST /api/needs-user
docs.text:
The needs_user hint a tab shows now, which browser_resume polls (#376). 

{ "tabId": 12 }
Returns { "ok": true, "tabId": 12, "needs_user": { "reason": "sign_in", … } }, with needs_user: null when the tab shows none.

docs.title: GET /api/workflows
docs.text:
List workflow files bundled in the kitsune/workflows package directory. 

{ "workflows": ["gmail-template-draft", "test", "wp-html"], "directory": ".../site-packages/kitsune/workflows" }

docs.title: POST /api/workflow
docs.text:
Execute a named workflow from the workflows directory. 

{ "name": "test", "variables": { "url": "https://example.com" }, "tabId": 12 }
tabId (optional) is the tab for steps that name none. Workflows are .md files with JSON code blocks. Variables use {{name}} syntax. Returns { "workflow": "test", "steps": 4, "results": [...], "progress": [...], "status": "ok", "summary": "..." }, plus newTabs as for POST /api/batch. A workflow stops at its first failed step; progress marks the rest skipped (see Container progress). A workflow that did not finish ok adds call and resume_token for POST /api/resume; resuming is refused if the workflow file changed.

docs.title: History and bookmarks (POST)
docs.text: POST /api/history-search {query, limit?, since?} (since in epoch milliseconds), POST /api/history-visits {url}, and POST /api/bookmarks-search {query, limit?} back the history tools; see History and bookmarks. The bridge adds the policy scope.

docs.title: POST /api/cache
docs.text:
Control the response cache (pageText is cached for 5s by default; tab inventories are always read fresh).

Clear cache: { "action": "clear" } Check status: { "action": "status" } → { "entries": 3, "ttl": 5 } Set TTL: { "action": "ttl", "seconds": 10 } — seconds must be a non-negative number; anything else answers HTTP 400 and keeps the current TTL.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: All endpoints return { "error": "message" } on failure; classified failures add code, retryable, hint, and state (see Action errors). The matching MCP tools mark these results isError: true (see MCP error results). Common errors: - "Kitsune extension not connected. Open Firefox or Zen and make sure the Kitsune extension is loaded." (extension_disconnected) — extension not loaded or browser closed - "Extension disconnected" (extension_disconnected) — extension dropped mid-command (fails fast, no timeout wait) - "No active tab found" (browser_window_unavailable) — no normal browser window the extension can use - "Command timed out after Ns" (timeout) — extension didn't respond in time - "Cannot access browser internal page: about:..." (restricted_page) — can't inject into restricted pages

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text:
Same tasks, same model (Claude Opus 5.5), same tool allowlist, one run per task:

  • Your tab stays in front. While a user was in the browser, Kitsune v0.7.2 never moved their view in 28 tasks. Playwright MCP, which was not built to share a browser with a person, moved it in 26.
  • It costs less. On the tasks both solved, Kitsune cost 0.56 to 0.97 times as much as Playwright MCP.
  • It solves about as many. Kitsune solved 96 of 98 tasks, Playwright MCP 98. Kitsune's two misses are one task, "go back to the tab I was on", in two variants: the user's tab stayed in front, but the agent's own tab was still its current tab, and that is what the grader checks.

See the v0.7.2 report and the full reports. scripts/benchmark_chart.py draws the chart from the report's numbers.

docs.title: How is it different?
docs.text:
If you want to… Consider Hand tasks to an agent in the Firefox-family browser you are using, with background tabs and read/draft/act modes Kitsune Debug or profile pages in Firefox (debugger, profiler, deep protocol access) Mozilla Firefox DevTools MCP, which attaches to a Firefox started with remote-debugging flags Test across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in browsers it launches Playwright MCP; Kitsune uses the same core tools, so prompts carry over Drive the Chrome you already use A Chromium extension MCP such as Browser MCP

Kitsune connects through an extension and a local bridge, so Firefox needs no startup flags. Other Firefox extensions also reuse your logins; Kitsune focuses on sharing the browser with you while the agent works. Positioning has the full comparison.

docs.title: Checkpoint and resume
docs.text: A browser_batch, browser_parallel or browser_workflow call that did not finish ok can be continued with browser_resume (#33, #115), and so can a direct call that stopped on needs_user (Direct calls, #376). One rule holds throughout: resuming never sends a write again after it ran ok, and sends a write whose outcome is unknown again only after the caller observed that it did not take effect.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text:
A container call whose status is not ok (unknown, held, failed or skipped, including a container_timeout) keeps a checkpoint. Its response adds two fields to results, progress, status and summary (Container progress):

{ "results": [{ "ok": true }, { "error": "Command timed out after 30s", "code": "timeout", "retryable": false }],
  "progress": [
    { "index": 0, "action": "click", "tabId": 3, "status": "ok" },
    { "index": 1, "action": "submitForm", "tabId": 3, "status": "unknown" },
    { "index": 2, "action": "pageText", "tabId": 3, "status": "skipped" }],
  "status": "unknown",
  "summary": "3 commands: 1 ok, 1 unknown, 1 skipped. ...",
  "call": 42,
  "resume_token": "x3J..." }
  • call is the audit call id of the container (Audit log). resume_token is random (secrets, 24 bytes). Resuming needs both, so knowing a call id from the audit log is not enough.
  • Checkpoints live in bridge memory only. They are never written to disk or to the audit log, and a bridge restart loses them. The bridge keeps at most 20 (the oldest is dropped first). Each expires 30 minutes after its call ended.
  • A checkpoint holds the call's commands (typed values included), results and step records, and only a hash of the token. All of it is dropped on expiry, when the checkpoint is pushed out by newer ones, when a resume finishes ok or stops on an internal error, and on bridge shutdown.
  • A call that finished ok has no checkpoint and no call/resume_token fields.

docs.title: browser_resume
docs.text:
browser_resume(call, resume_token, observed=None, wait=120)

The tool is in the core capability group (#376; it was in automation), so the default KITSUNE_CAPS=core has it. For a container call it sends POST /api/resume with {"call", "resume_token", "observed"}, a route of both core and automation; wait is not used. A direct call's checkpoint is resumed by the MCP server itself (Direct calls).

The response has the shape of the original call: results, progress, status and summary for every command, plus workflow and steps for a workflow. If the resumed call still did not finish ok, the response carries the same call and a new resume_token, and the old token stops working. The checkpoint is replaced and expires 30 minutes after this resume. If it finished ok, the checkpoint is dropped.

A resume has a fixed 300 s deadline, because the MCP server cannot see the stored commands. That applies even when the original batch allowed longer waits. At the deadline it stops like any container (container_timeout), and the response carries a new checkpoint. The tool waits past the deadline plus the settle time, so the partial report arrives.

docs.title: Step paths
docs.text:
Steps are named by their progress path:

Path Step "2" top-level command 2 of a batch or workflow "0.1.3" step 3 of sequence 1 of the parallel at command 0 (progress[0].sequences[1][3]) "1.2" step 2 of the sequence at command 1

Paths nest: "0.1.3.0" is step 0 of a sequence at that parallel step.

docs.title: What each step does
docs.text:
Last record Resume ok Not sent again; its stored result is reused. Its progress record adds resumed: "kept". Exception: an ok read inside a sequence runs again when a later step of that sequence that will run uses its result through ${$N...}, so that step reads fresh state skipped Sent: it never started failed Sent again (retryable: true, or nothing was dispatched) held Sent again through ask-before-act, so it stays held while ask mode is on and the call stops there. After confirming it with a direct call, report it "applied" unknown read Sent again unknown write Refused until observed reports it: "not_applied" sends it again, "applied" marks it ok without sending it

Writes are the bridge's write actions, plus anything that runs agent JavaScript (js, waitForResult, syncBarrier, an if/while condition), cookies, page storage, the clipboard, downloads and broadcast. navigate, newTab, closeTab and switchTab count as writes: sending them again could reset a form, duplicate a tab or close the wrong one.

sequence and parallel commands are resumed step by step. Other blocks (if, while, try, retry, broadcast) are resumed as one step. If one of them is not ok but a write in it already ran ok (for example the click before a failing find in a try, or the condition of an if whose branch failed), it is never sent again. It accepts only "applied", and resume refuses until the caller gives it.

observed maps step paths to "applied" or "not_applied". It is accepted only for unknown, held and failed steps. For a failed or held step, "not_applied" does the same as leaving it out. There is no default for an unknown write. Every entry is checked before anything is sent.

Every resumed step goes through the current policy again: read-only mode, the URL allow and deny lists and ask-before-act. A confirmation token is never honored inside a resume. A step reported "applied" is not sent, so nothing reaches the page.

A resumed batch keeps stopOnWarning, but does not stop again at a step it kept. A batch or sequence still stops at a held step. Steps after the stop that ran ok earlier stay ok (resumed: "kept") in progress and in the next checkpoint.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
A workflow checkpoint keeps the SHA-256 hash of the workflow file it ran. If the file changed or is gone, the resume is refused with workflow_changed and nothing is sent. A resume runs the stored commands, so changing the variables is not possible.

A batch or workflow checkpoint also keeps the call's default tab (tabId, by default the current tab of the MCP server that ran it). Resumed steps that name no tab run there, even if the agent has opened or selected another tab since.

docs.title: Parallel
docs.text:
Each sequence of a resumed parallel continues from its own records: a sequence that finished ok sends nothing, the others continue concurrently. The sequences keep the tab claims they made in the first run, including tabs claimed through ${$N.tabId}. Before the sequences start, each one with steps left is refused, with each of those steps failing and none sent, when:

  • tab_closed: a tab its remaining steps act on was closed (checked with getTabs). A closed tab is never replaced. If the tabs cannot be listed, the sequence is refused with that error.
  • tab_owned: another sequence of this parallel claimed a tab it writes.
  • tab_claimed: another call's parallel that is in progress writes one of its tabs (state.call).

The other sequences resume as usual. A refused sequence keeps its records, so a later resume can try it again.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every error below except resume_failed sends nothing and leaves the checkpoint as it was.

code HTTP Meaning checkpoint_not_found 404 No checkpoint for call: it finished ok, expired, was pushed out, is being resumed by another request, stopped on an internal error, or the bridge restarted resume_token_invalid 403 resume_token does not match the checkpoint's latest token workflow_changed 409 The workflow file changed since the call (state.workflow) observed_invalid 400 observed names a step that is ok, skipped, a sequence/parallel block or does not exist, or gives a value the step does not accept (state.steps: step, reason, accepts) observed_required 400 A step needs an observation (state.steps: step, action, tabId, status, accepts) resume_failed 200 The resume stopped on an internal error. progress reports what ran, steps in progress may have taken effect, and the checkpoint is dropped

A direct call's resume adds current_tab_changed and answers observed_invalid and resume_token_invalid itself (Direct calls).

The per-sequence tab_closed, tab_owned and tab_claimed errors appear in results like other step errors. No error or audit entry contains the resume token, typed values, JavaScript or stored results.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text: Resumed steps are audited like other container steps, with parent: {call, path, resumed: true}. call is the original call's id. Typed values stay redacted and JavaScript bodies are dropped (Audit log). A step reported "applied" gets one entry with params.observed: "applied" and params.sent: false. Steps kept from the first run get no new entry. The token never appears in the audit log or the bridge log.

docs.title: Direct calls
docs.text:
A direct tool call that stops on needs_user and was not resolved in the call keeps a checkpoint (#376), except for tab handoff requests: an ask-before-act hold on a client without elicitation, or one whose approval prompt was declined, dismissed or got no answer in time, and a browser_ask_user request (below). Its result adds call and resume_token, and its hint says what browser_resume does with it:

{ "error": "The action needs approval; nothing was done", "code": "needs_user", "retryable": false,
  "state": { "reason": "approval", "detail": "confirmation_required", "decision": "declined", "approval": "elicitation", "…": "…" },
  "call": 57, "resume_token": "Qk9…",
  "hint": "The held action did not run: the user declined it … browser_resume(call, resume_token) asks them again …" }
  • call is the audit call id the bridge gave the held request: its audit entry carries it as call (Audit log), so it never names a container call. A resume that is still pending keeps the same call and returns a new resume_token; the hold it made again has an audit entry with its own call.
  • The MCP server that made the call keeps the checkpoint, under the rules for container checkpoints: in memory only, at most 20 (the oldest is dropped first), each expiring 30 minutes after its call or its last resume, with only a SHA-256 hash of the token. It holds the tool, its arguments (without confirm_token), the held result without its confirm token, and the current tab the call ran on. It is dropped when a resume no longer stops on needs_user. It is lost when that MCP server restarts, and another MCP client cannot resume it: the bridge answers checkpoint_not_found, and the agent calls the tool again.
  • Holds that cannot be approved get no checkpoint: read and draft modes (state.approvable: false), and tools without confirm_token. Container results never get a direct checkpoint. Tab handoff requests also have no resume checkpoint: repeat the exact request with its valid confirm token, or make a fresh request.

browser_resume(call, resume_token, wait=120) runs the tool again with its stored arguments, from the held request:

  • Nothing of the call that ran ok is sent again. The call restarts at the held request: browser_fill_form does not fill the fields before the held one again, and browser_type(submit=true) held at its Enter presses Enter without typing the text again (the bridge names the held request in state.action). Every other tool that takes confirm_token sends one write per call.
  • A resume grants nothing a new call would not. The held request goes through the current policy again, including ask-before-act and tab permissions. User-tab writes are read-only by default; a resume cannot grant ownership. If the hold no longer applies, the call runs without an approval, as calling the tool again would at that moment.
  • A resume never waits for a hold to lift. On a client with elicitation, a request held again is asked about in the approval prompt, which stays open up to wait seconds (at most the token's 120 s less 5 s); wait=0 asks nothing. Without elicitation the hold is checked once and the resume returns at once: needs_user again with a fresh confirm token and a new resume_token. Switching the user's view does not change tab permissions.
  • wait is 0 to 300 seconds (default 120); larger values are capped at 300. While the prompt is open, a call that sent a progressToken gets a progress notification every 10 s. The MCP server waits itself, between bridge requests, so no bridge request outlasts its own timeout; a client's tool-call timeout must allow wait plus the call itself.
  • The result is the tool's own result. Approved, declined (state.decision: "declined") and unanswered ("cancelled") work as in the call. While it still stops on needs_user, it carries the same call and a new resume_token, and the old token stops working.
  • A stop the page resolves has a check in kitsune.server.PAGE_STATE_CHECKS, which the resume polls every second for up to wait seconds before it runs the call again. While the check fails, the resume returns the stop again with a new resume_token, and nothing is sent. sign_in and human_check are checked by the tab's needs_user hint (/api/needs-user): resolved once the tab no longer shows one with that reason. A failed read is not resolved.

browser_ask_user keeps a checkpoint when there is something to wait for:

  • With elicitation, when the prompt was dismissed or got no answer in time (state.decision: "cancelled"), not when the user answered Can't. The resume asks the user again in the client's prompt, for up to wait seconds (at most 120), and returns the answer as the call would; wait=0 asks nothing.
  • Without elicitation, when it asks about sign_in or human_check and the tab showed that hint as it asked (state.evidence). The resume waits for the hint to be gone from the tab, then returns {"ok": true, "answer": "done", "via": "page", …}. Without such a hint there is nothing to watch, so the result has no resume_token: the agent asks in its reply.
  • The request itself never reaches the page, so a resume sends nothing to it either.

Errors of a direct call's resume send nothing and keep the checkpoint:

code Meaning current_tab_changed The call acts on the current tab, and the agent made another tab current since (state.tabId, state.currentTab). Make that tab current again with browser_tabs select, or call the tool again observed_invalid observed was given: a direct call has no steps to observe resume_token_invalid resume_token does not match the call's latest token

A resume whose call fails another way (its target is gone, the tab closed) returns that error, and the checkpoint is gone: check the page and call the tool again.

docs.title: Without browser_resume
docs.text: After a container's checkpoint is gone, resume by hand. Send a new batch that starts at the first record that is not ok, after observing the page for any unknown record. After a direct call's checkpoint is gone, call the tool again.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Default Meaning KITSUNE_CAPS core Comma-separated capability groups; all enables every group except storage and history, which read personal data and must be named KITSUNE_PUBLISH KITSUNE_CAPS Groups of the enabled tools that tools/list shows when a session starts; the others stay reachable through the gateway tools. See Finding tools without a restart KITSUNE_MODE act Task surface and per-request policy: read, draft, or act. See Task modes KITSUNE_HOME ~/.kitsune Data directory (0700) KITSUNE_HTTP_PORT 47651 Bridge HTTP API KITSUNE_WS_PORT 47652 Extension WebSocket. Change WS_URL in extension/background/background.js too KITSUNE_TOKEN — Override the token in ~/.kitsune/token KITSUNE_EXTENSION_DIR extension/ in a checkout Unpacked extension the bridge compares a developer build with, to report one that was edited but not reloaded, and whose WS_URL port it expects before the extension connects (Connection diagnosis) KITSUNE_NO_BRIDGE_RESTART Unset Set to 1 in the MCP server environment to skip automatic replacement of an outdated bridge KITSUNE_BRIDGE_IDLE_TIMEOUT 0 (never) Seconds without client activity before the bridge exits; see Idle shutdown KITSUNE_OUTPUT_DIR Unset Directory, in the MCP server environment, for relative filename arguments of the core tools; unset, they resolve against the client's first root, else the server's working directory (see Core tools) KITSUNE_OWNER_ID The MCP client's process Tab owner id of the MCP client, in the MCP server environment: the bridge records the tabs it opens as this client's and offers them after a server restart. Up to 64 letters, digits, ., _, : or -. Set it when the server runs through a launcher other than uv or uvx, such as a shell script or a Python wrapper. Give each MCP client its own value: clients with the same value share their tabs. See Tab owners KITSUNE_USER_TABS read-only Set to writable to allow this client to write user tabs; see Protecting your tabs for values and invalid-value errors KITSUNE_ASK_BEFORE_ACT Unset Set to 1 in the MCP server environment to start the bridge with ask-before-act locked on; the lock then persists in ask-before-act-locked under KITSUNE_HOME KITSUNE_HISTORY_ALLOW_DOMAINS Unset (every domain) Bridge: comma-separated domains (with subdomains) the history tools may return; see History and bookmarks KITSUNE_HISTORY_DENY_DOMAINS Unset (none) Bridge: comma-separated domains (with subdomains) the history tools never return; wins over the allow list KITSUNE_HISTORY_MAX_DAYS 30 Bridge: how many days back the history tools may look. browser_set_policy can only tighten these three KITSUNE_POST_ACTION_SNAPSHOT Enabled (deltas) Set to 0 in the bridge daemon environment and restart it to disable automatic post-action snapshots, full to return full snapshots instead of deltas, or text to add readable text lines to them

~/.kitsune/ holds:

File Content token Bearer token for the HTTP API (0600, created on first start) bridge.log Daemon output sessions/ Saved sessions, including cookies screenshots/ Screenshots ask-before-act-locked Present while ask-before-act is locked on (0600); delete it to unlock

docs.title: Setup from a checkout
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/junyeong-nero/kitsune ~/workspace/kitsune
cd ~/workspace/kitsune
uv sync

Register the checkout instead of the PyPI package so the client runs your working tree directly:

claude mcp add --scope user kitsune -- uv run --directory ~/workspace/kitsune kitsune

In JSON or TOML configs, use "command": "uv" with ["run", "--directory", "/Users/you/workspace/kitsune", "kitsune"]. Load the extension from the checkout's extension/manifest.json (that is the developer build). To try the signed variant locally, build it and load build/extension-signed/manifest.json the same way:

uv run python scripts/build_extension.py signed

To test the installed-package path of a branch, build both packages and run the server from their wheels; rebuild after you edit files:

uv build --all-packages
uvx --from dist/kitsune_browser_mcp-<version>-py3-none-any.whl \
    --with dist/kitsune_browser-<version>-py3-none-any.whl kitsune

(uvx --from ./packages/kitsune-browser-mcp kitsune instead runs the working tree's code, which uv installs editable.)

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Run the tests from the repository root:

uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -q
for test in tests/*.cjs; do node "$test"; done

The Python regression suite covers the MCP tool surface, snapshots, navigation waits, and bridge lifecycle; the Node harnesses cover content-script behavior such as refs, form filling, and password redaction. For an end-to-end check, load the extension in a supported browser and follow Try it; unit tests alone do not verify your live browser connection. File reproducible bugs in GitHub Issues, including the browser version, bridge build from browser_status, tool calls, and expected versus actual behavior. Use a minimal public or local page and redact secrets.

Tool definitions are resent with every model request, so their size is tracked: uv run python scripts/tool_schema_size.py reports the compact JSON size of each core tool in two views: the full definition, and the definition with its description cut to the first paragraph, as some clients (Claude Code --bare) send it. A test fails until --update records a change in tests/tool_schema_sizes.json. The same test fails when the core total grows past TOTAL_BUDGETS or FIRST_PARAGRAPH_BUDGETS, or any single tool past TOOL_BUDGET, or the server instructions of a mode past INSTRUCTIONS_BUDGETS; raise a budget only deliberately. The core tools are Playwright MCP's, published verbatim, and tests/test_playwright_tools.py checks the default tools/list against src/kitsune/playwright_tools.json. The Kitsune-owned tools' published input schemas omit the title keywords pydantic generates (KitsuneMCP.list_tools), and tests/test_tool_schema_titles.py checks that they still accept and reject the same arguments. They also publish an optional parameter whose default is null as its plain type instead of anyOf: [type, null], and omit null and "" defaults. Calls are still validated against the pydantic models, so an explicit null still works and behaves as omitted; tests/test_tool_schema_optionals.py checks this for every tool. Every client sends input schemas in full, so parameters are documented there (Annotated[..., Field(description=...)]), not in Args: blocks. A tool's first paragraph says what it does and what a caller must know. The Kitsune-owned action tools share one contract (ref, element, wait, expect, confirm_token, first; confirm_token is the approval fallback for clients without elicitation), documented once in browser_check's parameter descriptions; the other action tools say in their first paragraph that ok means dispatched, name expect and point to browser_check rather than repeating it. tab_id is described wherever it is accepted. tests/test_tool_first_paragraph.py checks these rules for every Kitsune-owned tool.

docs.title: Real-browser suites
docs.text:
The opt-in real-browser suites (tests/test_real_browser*.py) run against a real Firefox, Zen or LibreWolf. They cover action races, tab unloads and reconnects (test_real_browser.py), tabs opened by target=_blank clicks with popups allowed and with the default popup blocker (test_real_browser_opened_tabs.py), every read tool on empty 404 and 500 pages (test_real_browser_error_pages.py), and which form or button an action picks on a page with repeated controls (test_real_browser_action_targets.py). They are skipped unless KITSUNE_E2E_BROWSER names the browser binary. A full run takes several minutes, depending on the host and browser; run one suite when iterating:

KITSUNE_E2E_BROWSER=/Applications/Zen.app/Contents/MacOS/zen \
  uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_real_browser*.py' -v

Use -p test_real_browser_error_pages.py (or another file name) to run one suite. Each test class starts a headless browser on a new temporary profile and HOME, plus its own bridge and fixture site on spare ports, and kills them afterwards. Your browser profiles and running bridge are not touched. The suites run a copy of the extension whose bridge port is rewritten to the test bridge. The browser does not start if any script in the copy still names port 47652, or if the test bridge would use that port. The shared harness, tests/real_browser_harness.py, documents how to add a suite, including how to choose the profile prefs (browser defaults or popups allowed).

To keep evidence from a failing run, set KITSUNE_E2E_ARTIFACTS to a directory:

KITSUNE_E2E_BROWSER=/Applications/Zen.app/Contents/MacOS/zen \
  KITSUNE_E2E_ARTIFACTS=/tmp/kitsune-e2e-artifacts \
  uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_real_browser*.py' -v

Each failing test, or failing class setup, writes one directory under kitsune-e2e-<UTC time>-<pid>/<module.Class>/ and prints its path to stderr. timeline.jsonl puts the harness's bridge requests, the fixture server's request events and the browser's top-level navigation events (load start/stop, location changes, tab open/close) on one wall clock, so a slow page load can be told apart from a slow fixture reply. For each fixture request it records when the request was received and then either request-handled (the handler returned and the server flushed its reply) or request-failed with the exception type (for example BrokenPipeError after the browser dropped the connection; the error still reaches the server). Both are server-side only and do not show that the browser received the reply. Only bridge requests sent through the harness's call() are in the timeline; open_tab (/api/new-tab) is, but suites that send harness._request directly (test_real_browser.py, test_real_browser_protected_tabs.py, test_real_browser_submit_form.py, test_real_browser_connection_diagnostics.py) appear only in bridge.log. Harness and fixture events share one buffer of 4000 events per test process; summary.json reports how many events recorded since the class started were evicted (droppedSinceClassStart, with complete: false when any were) and, separately, all evictions in the process (droppedInProcess). browser.log and bridge.log hold the last 256 KiB of the owned browser's and bridge's output, resources.json the load average and ps samples of the test runner, the bridge and the browser's process group, and summary.json what was collected. Passing classes write nothing; a class keeps at most five failures; nothing under the directory is ever deleted by the harness. The timeline and summaries hold no headers, request bodies or page contents, and URLs in them keep only a loopback origin and path. The two log tails are copied as the owned processes wrote them, with the bridge token, Authorization, Bearer and token= values redacted; with the variable set, the owned bridge writes its log unbuffered so that it is current when a test fails. Without the variable the suites run exactly as before.

docs.text: To publish a new version to PyPI, see Releasing.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
extension/          WebExtension (manifest v2, Gecko)
packages/kitsune-browser-mcp/  The MCP server's PyPI package: pins kitsune-browser[mcp], adds the commands
src/kitsune/        The kitsune-browser package (the repository root's pyproject.toml)
  server.py         MCP server: registers the tools on FastMCP, within KITSUNE_CAPS and KITSUNE_MODE
  tools.py          The agent tools (Kitsune's own) without MCP code; playwright_tools.py has the core group
  browser.py        Python API (kitsune.connect, Browser, Tab); errors.py has its exceptions
  bridge_client.py  Bridge requests and connection errors; starts the bridge on demand
  bridge.py         Bridge daemon (HTTP API + WebSocket)
  workflows/        Named workflows for browser_workflow
docs/               Documentation site (mkdocs.yml), API reference, scraping playbooks

docs.title: Credits
docs.text: Kitsune started as a fork of ZenLink and ZenLink-MCP by Jay-Quan (MIT). Changes since the fork: token auth, Host and origin checks, no CORS, on-demand shared daemon, one package, browser_* tool names, ~/.kitsune data directory, macOS support, mcp<2 pin.
