docs.title: Connection, tabs and pages
docs.text: Symptom Check Any connection problem Call browser_status and follow diagnosis.hint; each diagnosis.code is listed in Connection diagnosis. It never shows the token extension_disconnected (extension_connected: false) Extension installed and enabled in the browser profile you opened? Developer build: browser restarted (temporary add-on gone)? It reconnects within 15 s of a bridge start; the first tool call after the MCP server starts a bridge waits up to 16 s for it extension_version_mismatch The extension and server versions differ; install the matching extension or update the server, then reload open tabs. state.reason: "stale_developer_build": the developer build's files changed since the browser loaded them; reload it in about:debugging browser_window_unavailable The browser runs without a normal window Kitsune can use; open one, or allow Kitsune in private windows (about:addons → Kitsune → Run in Private Windows) new_tab_stalled (new tab stays about:blank / complete after its load timeout), navigation_stalled (same, after browser_navigate) The tab was created or navigated, but no loaded destination could be confirmed. Retrying will not fix it: the browser needs an update, a restart or another fix first. Do not keep creating tabs or navigating; inspect or close the returned tab. Run browser_status(diagnostics=true) for browser build diagnostics. A mismatch is evidence that a browser restart is pending, not proof of this failure's cause; unknown is not a clean bill of health. Tell the user and ask them to save work and restart or update the browser, or fix it another way; once they say it is fixed, check status and list tabs again (IDs may change). In #366, old Contents.bak files were still mapped after an app update; restarting recovered loading without a Kitsune change. Reloading the extension or bridge does not restart the browser host_permission_denied not_granted: allow site access in about:addons → Kitsune → Permissions. restricted_domain: Firefox keeps extensions off Mozilla sites such as addons.mozilla.org; use another tab "needs the Kitsune developer extension build" The signed build cannot run agent-supplied JavaScript; load the developer build bridge_unavailable (Kitsune bridge did not start, exited at startup) state.logExcerpt shows the bridge's last log line; see ~/.kitsune/bridge.log, or run kitsune-bridge start in a terminal to see the error. state.reason: "not_responding": the bridge hangs; run kitsune-bridge stop and retry port_conflict state.port is held by another program (lsof -nP -iTCP:47651 -sTCP:LISTEN), or KITSUNE_WS_PORT differs from the extension's WS_URL token_mismatch (401 Missing or invalid token) KITSUNE_TOKEN or KITSUNE_HOME set in one client but not in the daemon (or the other way round) user_tab_read_only Nothing ran and no approval is offered. Open the URL in a tab of the agent's own before writing, or explicitly request a handoff. Reads work on any tab; those that scroll it (element or full-page screenshots, find load_more) only while it is not shown needs_user with state.detail: "tab_handoff" The handoff was declined, invalidated or needs client approval after the browser prompt timed out. Follow state.message and the hint; repeat the exact request with its token only after approval, or open an agent tab. Handoff requests do not have resume checkpoints needs_user with state.reason: "approval" (state.detail: confirmation_required, or legacy user_tab) Nothing ran: the call needs your approval. On a client with elicitation (Claude Code 2.1.76 and later, Codex) you get a prompt; Approve runs that one call. No prompt appeared and the result has state.approval: "token": the client lacks elicitation, so the agent should tell you state.message and repeat the call with confirm_token, the fallback for such clients, only after you agree. Or have it work in a tab of its own. See Approving held actions needs_user with state.decision: "declined" or "cancelled" declined: you declined the approval prompt, or answered Can't to browser_ask_user; nothing ran, and the agent should not ask again for the same thing. cancelled: the prompt was dismissed or closed unanswered (an approval prompt closes 5 s before its approval would expire). If you still want it done, the agent calls browser_resume(call, resume_token) when supplied, which asks you again. Handoff requests have no resume token: make a fresh request needs_user with state.reason: "agent_request" The agent asked you with browser_ask_user; state.detail says for what (sign_in, human_check, trusted_input, other) and state.message what to do. Do it, then answer Done in the client's prompt, or tell the agent in chat on a client without elicitation. For a sign-in or CAPTCHA the tab shows, the agent can call browser_resume, which waits until it is gone. See When the agent needs you A result has a needs_user hint (reason: sign_in, human_check, trusted_input) Kitsune saw something only you can do; nothing was held, and the call's own result stands. If the agent cannot go on, it asks you (browser_ask_user). sign_in: sign in yourself (password fields stay redacted from the agent); human_check: complete the CAPTCHA; trusted_input: click the control yourself, or let the agent try browser_trusted_click. See needs_user hints browser_resume returns needs_user again at once for an approval Without elicitation a resume checks the hold once and never waits for you; it continues only if the hold no longer applies. Approve in chat, and the agent repeats the call with confirm_token. With wait=0 it asks nothing; resume with a wait to be asked Cannot access browser internal page about: pages are off-limits to extensions; switch to a normal tab A click returns dispatched: true but the page does not react (outcome_not_observed, target still visible) Some pages accept only trusted input and ignore Kitsune's synthetic events. Check the page with browser_snapshot first, then try one browser_trusted_click on the same target and verify it with a read. It needs the browse capability, moves your real cursor for the click (then back, unless restore_pointer=False for a hover menu that closes when the pointer leaves) and, on macOS, needs pyobjc Quartz or cliclick plus Accessibility permission; on Linux, needs xdotool in an X11 session (not Wayland), and HiDPI X11 scaling is not compensated, so the click may land off by the scale factor. Page zoom is compensated, and a target covered by another element (an overlay or banner) returns target_not_at_point without clicking. Kitsune never switches to it on its own A hover returns ok: true but the menu or row controls it should reveal stay hidden browser_hover sends pointer and mouse events, including pointerenter/mouseenter to each entered ancestor, but it cannot trigger CSS :hover, which follows only the real pointer. Use browser_trusted_click with restore_pointer=False on an element where a click is harmless, which leaves your real pointer there, or ask the user to point at it. See POST /api/hover A press-and-hold button, a tile that reveals controls after a moment of hovering, or a custom slider or drag handle does not react Long-press controls need hold_ms on browser_click (or browser_trusted_click), and hover-intent controls need duration_ms (and steps) on browser_hover; the core tools accept both without listing them. A handle that captures the pointer (setPointerCapture) rejects synthetic pointers: on macOS, browser_trusted_drag (browse capability) drags it with your real pointer A background tab's snapshot is empty, or a menu item a click just opened returns hidden_or_covered with state.hiddenTab or state.inPopup Results from a hidden tab carry visibilityState: "hidden"; tabs the agent opens are in the background by default, so their results usually carry it. Some pages render lazily, or do not paint menus and popups, while their tab is hidden (#259, #260). Events dispatched to an unpainted item still work, so act on it if it belongs to the control you meant and check the effect. If content never appears, Kitsune's browser_tabs select with tab_id shows the tab and switches the user's own view, so ask the user first; it is refused with user_active while they use the tab they would leave. The core browser_tabs select only makes a tab current. See Snapshot readiness browser_trusted_click returns browser_not_at_point (macOS) Another app's window, not the browser's, is at the click point, typically because the browser is in full screen on another Space; nothing was clicked. Switch to the browser's Space or leave full screen, then retry. See browser_trusted_click browser_trusted_click near the top of a page returns browser_not_at_point while the browser is in full screen (macOS) Verified on macOS 26.5.1 with Zen 1.24b (#336): the hidden menu bar is not in the way. Zen's own full-screen strip, a second Zen window over the top 68 points of the screen, refuses with state.reason: "other_browser_window" (#431). While the menu bar shows (the pointer rests at the top edge), the menu bar refuses with "other_window" (state.app: "Window Server") and the strip moves down below it, to 98 points. Nothing was clicked. Scroll the target further down, or leave full screen, then retry. To check what macOS reports there, run KITSUNE_E2E_BROWSER=/Applications/Zen.app/Contents/MacOS/zen KITSUNE_E2E_TRUSTED_INPUT=1 uv run --extra macos python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_real_browser_fullscreen_menubar.py -v while nobody uses the machine; it puts its own browser window in full screen, makes no click and prints the windows at a few points near the top. KITSUNE_E2E_REVEAL_MENU_BAR=1 also moves the pointer (no click) to the top edge to show the menu bar, then back A trusted click, type, key press or drag returns tab_not_shown, or browser_tabs lists loaded tabs as about:blank (Zen) The browser window shows no page: on a brand-new Zen profile, its first-run welcome screen hides the tab area until it is finished (#360). Nothing was clicked. Finish or close the welcome screen, then retry; tabs loaded while it was open keep reporting about:blank until they navigate again "Continue with Google" or another sign-in button opens no popup, or the site says "Something went wrong" With Firefox's default popup blocker, synthetic clicks cannot open OAuth/SSO popups (the click result may have a popup_blocked warning with state.reason: "script_popup"); ask the user to click, or use a trusted click. See Sign-in popups (OAuth/SSO) stale ref, call browser_snapshot again Take a fresh snapshot of the same tab_id and use its new refs Bridge updated but browser behavior is unchanged Reload the extension, then reload affected pages so their content scripts update too Restart the daemon Run kitsune-bridge stop with the same source as your clients (uvx --from git+… or uv run in a checkout); the next tool call starts it again. This briefly affects all clients sharing it value-attribute selectors are disabled … A sensitive field on the page has a value attribute; target it by ref, label, or a selector that does not test value

docs.title: Sign-in popups (OAuth/SSO)
docs.text:
"Continue with Google", "Sign in with Apple" and similar buttons open the provider's sign-in in a popup window or tab with window.open. With the default popup blocker (dom.disable_open_during_load=true, see Popup-blocked links), Firefox allows that only during user activation, that is, a real click or key press. browser_click dispatches synthetic DOM events without user activation, so the popup is blocked or the site's sign-in script fails: no window opens, or the page shows an error such as "Something went wrong. Please try again." Ordinary buttons on the same page still work. Kitsune reopens only blocked target="_blank" links (see Popup-blocked links). When the button's script calls window.open during the click and the popup blocker refuses it, the click result has a popup_blocked warning with state.reason: "script_popup" (see Script-opened popups). A script that fails before calling window.open, opens the popup later, or runs on a page whose Content Security Policy blocks Kitsune's wrapper gives no warning, so the click can still look successful or end in outcome_not_observed. When a refused popup is an OAuth, OpenID Connect or SAML sign-in request, the result also has a needs_user hint with reason sign_in (see When the agent needs you).

There are two ways through:

  1. Ask the user to click (recommended). The agent asks the user to click the button (browser_ask_user), waits for them, then lists tabs with browser_tabs to find the popup or tab that opened and continues there by tab_id. The user may also have to finish the provider's sign-in (account chooser, password, two-factor). This is the default to prefer because the browser is shared (#139): a trusted click moves your real pointer, may show the target tab and can take focus.
  2. browser_trusted_click. A real OS click has user activation, so the popup opens. It needs the browse capability and a visible browser window. On macOS a browser in full screen on another Space is not visible from the agent's Space, and focus=True may not switch to it: the call then returns browser_not_at_point without clicking, so ask the user to switch to the browser's Space (or leave full screen) and retry. Its result does not list opened_tabs, so find the popup with browser_tabs. Kitsune never switches to it on its own. On Linux it needs xdotool in an X11 session. On macOS, set it up once:
  3. Install a click backend: register the server with uvx --from 'kitsune-browser-mcp[macos]' kitsune (pyobjc Quartz; the extra installs nothing on other platforms), or run brew install cliclick so cliclick is on the PATH your MCP client passes to the server.
  4. Grant Accessibility permission to the app running the bridge, usually the terminal or MCP client app that started it (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility).
  5. Run kitsune-bridge stop with the same source as your clients so that the next start picks up the change. The click runs in the shared bridge, and the bridge runs with the Python (sys.executable) and PATH of whichever MCP server started it first. Adding the extra to one client's command does nothing until the bridge starts again from that client, so make the next tool call from it, or add the extra to every client.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Once installed and your tabs are listed, ask your agent:

Open a new tab, search for today's weather near Suseong Lake in Daegu, and summarize the forecast with a link to the source. Leave the tab open.

Or try:

  • “Open Hacker News and summarize the top three stories with links.”
  • “Inspect this page's form and fill a draft. Don't submit it yet.”
  • “Capture a screenshot of this page and save it to a file.”

A real screen recording of Claude Code and Zen on the live Google sites, sped up while the agent thinks (full 38-second video).

A typical tool sequence looks like this (Python-style pseudocode; these are MCP calls made by your agent; to drive the browser from your own code, see the Python API):

browser_tabs(action="new", url="https://example.com")  # the new tab becomes current
browser_snapshot()
# Inspect the returned snapshot, then use a ref from that result:
# browser_click(target="<latest ref>", element="More information")
browser_take_screenshot(filename="/tmp/kitsune-example.png")

Open a dedicated tab first (browser_tabs new) so the tools act on it. Until there is one, reads act on the active tab, and writes and navigations that name no tab fail with no_current_tab instead of acting on it. You and the agent share the browser: the agent's tabs open in the background, it closes only tabs it opened unless you approve, and it backs off from a tab you are using (see Shared browser). Ask the agent to confirm before submitting forms, sending messages, purchasing, or deleting data. Page content is untrusted input, not permission to take additional actions; see Security.

docs.title: Your tabs and approvals
docs.text:
• Your tabs. Writes to your tabs fail at once with user_tab_read_only, without a prompt. The agent opens its own tab instead, or asks for yours with a reason. You see the request in the toolbar popup (its badge shows a count) and approve or decline it there; after 30 seconds the agent's client asks you instead. An approved tab is the agent's until you press Take back or its session ends. It does not give the agent your real mouse or keyboard. To let the agent write to your tabs without asking, set KITSUNE_USER_TABS=writable (Protecting your tabs).
  • Risky actions. With the opt-in ask-before-act policy, submitting forms, payment pages, JavaScript and cookie access need your approval. Claude Code and Codex ask you in their own prompt, so the approval never passes through the agent. Other clients get a one-time token the agent should show you first; it guards against accidents, not against an agent that repeats the call on its own (Approving held actions).
  • Things only you can do. For a sign-in, a CAPTCHA or a choice that is yours to make, the agent asks you (browser_ask_user) and carries on when you are done (When the agent needs you).

docs.title: Protecting your tabs
docs.text:
Every tab is readable, but user tabs and other clients' tabs are read-only. Writes, scrolling, hovering, focusing, navigation, reload and close fail immediately with user_tab_read_only (retryable: false), without an approval prompt. The error names state.tabId, state.index (the browser_tabs list index) and state.action. Open the URL in a tab of the agent's own (browser_tabs action=new) before writing. Alternatively, browser_tabs action=request with an index or tab_id and a reason asks for a session-scoped handoff. Approval is browser-first (the toolbar popup), then client fallback after 30 seconds. A grant permits DOM/browser operations, not trusted/native OS input; it does not select or activate the tab. Approving also releases text you left in a focused field of that tab, so the agent can finish a form you started there. The user can Take back in the popup; session end or bridge/extension disconnection also returns it. Agent-created tabs keep their persistent ownership. Other clients' tabs cannot be transferred.

Snapshots, ordinary find, DOM reads, console/network reads and viewport screenshots can read your tabs without scrolling, focusing or switching your view; the agent's browser_tabs select makes any of them its current tab for that, without showing it. Reading a discarded tab reloads it in the background. find load_more and element/full-page screenshots scroll the page, so on a tab the agent cannot write they run only while the tab is not shown, and put its scroll position back afterwards; on the tab you are looking at they are refused. The current marker always identifies the agent's current tab, regardless of ownership; selection is not an ownership grant. On an owned tab, trusted user input still pauses writes with the existing retryable user_active response. Text you leave in a focused field pauses them until you leave the field or give the page no input for 10 s.

User-tab setting: KITSUNE_USER_TABS accepts read-only (the default) or writable, ignoring surrounding whitespace and letter case. With writable, this client may write user and other clients' tabs without changing ownership; user_active, task-mode limits and ask-before-act still apply. Invalid explicit values (including an empty string) stop MCP startup with a configuration error, rather than weakening protection. Python uses kitsune.connect(user_tabs="writable"); it does not read this environment setting. Omitting user_tabs means read-only.

The deprecated aliases KITSUNE_HOLD_VIEWED_TAB and KITSUNE_PROTECT_USER_TABS (and Python's hold_viewed_tab and protect_user_tabs) were removed after the 0.7.2 alias release. The environment variables are now ignored without a warning, so a client that set either to 0 is read-only again until it sets KITSUNE_USER_TABS=writable; the Python arguments raise TypeError.

The client sends only X-Kitsune-User-Tabs: read-only|writable to the bridge. Missing headers default to read-only; invalid values reject the request with HTTP 400 (invalid_user_tabs) before any action. Header names are case-insensitive: the client replaces any extra spelling with its configured permission. Multiple occurrences (even identical values) and comma-combined values are rejected, never resolved by order. Old X-Kitsune-Hold-Viewed-Tab and X-Kitsune-Protect-User-Tabs headers are ignored, not permission grants: upgrade old clients to use the new header. Tool arguments cannot override it. The bridge's process environment does not set permissions for its clients.

See Tab permissions.

docs.title: When the agent needs you
docs.text:
Some steps only you can take: signing in, a CAPTCHA, a button that ignores the agent's synthetic clicks. Kitsune points them out on its results as a needs_user hint (#376): a shown sign-in field or a sign-in popup the browser blocked (sign_in), a reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha or Turnstile frame (human_check), or a click only a real click works for (trusted_input). It reads only fields, frames and URLs for this, never the page's wording, and holds nothing for it: the agent may still type into a sign-in form you asked it to fill.

When the agent cannot go on, it asks you with browser_ask_user. On a client with elicitation you answer in the client's prompt: Done, or Can't. Otherwise the agent asks you in its reply; for a sign-in or CAPTCHA Kitsune sees on the tab, it can call browser_resume, which waits until the sign-in or CAPTCHA is gone from the tab, so you need not tell it you are done. Details are in the API reference.

docs.title: Ask-before-act
docs.text:
Ask-before-act is an opt-in policy. In this mode the bridge does not run form submits, submit-button clicks, clicks on buttons labeled like a submit or payment ("Place order", "Pay now", "결제하기"), Enter in form fields, browser_js and other agent JavaScript, cookie, session, and page-storage access, clipboard reads and writes, downloads, navigation to payment-like URLs, or page actions on such pages. Each such call needs your approval (see Approving held actions). The needs_user error (state.detail confirmation_required; until #376 that was its code) describes the pending action. On a client without elicitation it carries a single-use token, the fallback for approving there, that expires in 120 seconds and is bound to that exact action, its parameters, and its tab. Batch, retry, parallel, broadcast, and workflow commands never accept a token. Details are in the API reference.

There are two ways to turn it on:

  • browser_set_policy(ask=True): the agent can also turn this off again, so it only guards against accidents.
  • Locked: set KITSUNE_ASK_BEFORE_ACT=1 in the MCP server environment, or run kitsune-bridge start --ask-before-act. The policy can then only be tightened. A bridge that is already running keeps its policy, so run kitsune-bridge stop after changing the setting.

A locked bridge writes ~/.kitsune/ask-before-act-locked (under KITSUNE_HOME, readable only by you). While that file exists, every bridge starts locked, also after kitsune-bridge stop, an idle shutdown, or an MCP server replacing an outdated bridge, and also when the environment lacks KITSUNE_ASK_BEFORE_ACT=1. To unlock, remove the variable from every MCP server configuration, delete the file, and run kitsune-bridge stop.

The bridge checks the target before it acts, and the page can change in between (for example, it navigates to a checkout URL). Such a change is not caught.

[mcp_servers.kitsune.env]
KITSUNE_ASK_BEFORE_ACT = "1"

docs.title: Approving held actions
docs.text:
When ask-before-act holds a call for your approval, it returns needs_user with state.reason approval, and the held action does not run. User-tab writes instead fail with user_tab_read_only, without prompting. An explicit handoff request asks in the browser first, then falls back to the client. For ask-before-act, approval works as follows:

  • Clients with elicitation (Claude Code, Codex): Kitsune asks you in the client's own prompt, naming the action, its target, the call's arguments, the tab and why it was held. The agent's description of the target is labeled as the agent's. Approve, and Kitsune runs that one call; the agent never sees a token, so it cannot approve itself. Decline or dismiss it, and the agent gets needs_user with state.decision declined or cancelled. The prompt closes unanswered 5 seconds before the approval would expire. If you change your mind, the agent calls browser_resume, which asks you again and continues the call where it was held. Steps inside batches, parallel calls and workflows are not asked about: the agent repeats the held step as a direct call, which asks you.
  • Clients without elicitation: the error carries a token (state.approval token), and the agent should ask you, then repeat the call with confirm_token. That token goes back to the agent, so it guards against accidents only: the agent can repeat the call without asking. Have your MCP client prompt you before tool calls, or at least before calls that carry confirm_token. browser_resume on such a client checks the hold once and returns at once; it never waits for approval.

The bridge's audit log (browser_audit) records how each approved write was approved, approval: "elicitation" or "token". Details are in the API reference.

docs.title: Kitsune Scraping Playbooks
docs.text:
🤖 AI INSTRUCTION — READ THIS FIRST

Before writing any scraping batch sequence for a known site, check if a playbook exists in this directory. Playbooks contain verified selectors, working URL patterns, and documented workarounds from real scraping sessions. Using a playbook avoids re-discovering the same failures from scratch.

Available playbooks: - amazon.md — Bot detection, scroll-then-extract pattern - bestbuy.md — Lazy loading, scroll (scrollBy) fix, correct 2026 selectors - newegg.md — Silent category redirects, use /p/pl?d= search URL - bhphotovideo.md — CSS Modules hashed classes, wildcard selector pattern - ebay.md — Hidden placeholder cards, li.s-item gone, one-selector-per-field extraction without JS

If a playbook doesn't exist for the target site, create one after you solve it.

Playbook steps are /api/batch commands. Run them with the browser_batch MCP tool, which is in the automation group. Each step also needs its action's group: scroll is browse, pageText and pageInfo are read (for example KITSUNE_CAPS=core,automation,browse,read). The js and waitForResult actions need the developer extension build.

docs.title: 🛒 E-commerce Sites
docs.text: Site Main Challenge Key Fix Playbook Amazon Bot detection on JS injection Navigate normally, scroll, read rendered DOM only amazon.md Best Buy Intersection-observer lazy loading scroll amount:800 + correct selector .product-list-item bestbuy.md Newegg SubCategory URLs silently redirect Use /p/pl?d=keywords search URL instead newegg.md B&H Photo CSS Modules hashed class names [class*="product_"] wildcard + innerText parsing bhphotovideo.md eBay li.s-item returns 0; li.s-card adds 2 hidden placeholders ul.srp-results > li.s-card + one query per field ebay.md

docs.title: Lazy-loading sites (Best Buy, B&H)
docs.text:
Use scroll with amount: 800 (pixels, roughly one viewport height) to trigger intersection observers. Repeat with sleeps between to let cards render: 

{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 1500 },
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 1500 },
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 2000 }

docs.title: CSS Modules sites (B&H and any site with word_hash class names)
docs.text: Use [class*="prefix_"] wildcard selectors — the prefix before the underscore is stable across deploys. See bhphotovideo.md for the full pattern and a class-discovery snippet in the appendix.

docs.title: Bot-detection sites (Amazon)
docs.text:
• Use real browser navigation via navigate action only
  • Never use fetch() or XHR via the js action
  • Always scroll before extracting — let the page hydrate
  • Use waitForElement or waitForResult as your gate before extraction JS

docs.title: Silent redirect detection (Newegg and others)
docs.text:
Use expectTitle on the navigate action: 

{ "action": "navigate", "url": "https://...", "expectTitle": "gaming" }
Returns warning and redirected: true if the page title doesn't contain the expected string. No need for manual document.title checks.

docs.title: Adding a New Playbook
docs.text:
When you solve a new site, create docs/scraping-playbooks/SITENAME.md with: 1. Problem — what failed and why 2. Root Cause — the technical reason 3. What Does NOT Work — with code examples (saves future re-discovery) 4. What WORKS — full working sequence with copy-pasteable JSON 5. Key Selectors — table of verified selectors with a date stamp 6. Notes — edge cases, expiry warnings, gotchas

Then add a row to the table in this index file.

docs.title: Contributing Playbooks
docs.text:
Playbooks only help future agents and users if they're checked into the repo. After creating or updating a playbook:

  1. Stage the files: git add docs/scraping-playbooks/
  2. Commit: git commit -m "playbook: add <sitename> scraping workaround"
  3. Push: git push

If you're an AI agent, ask the user to commit and push on your behalf. If you're a human contributor, please push your playbooks — they save everyone (including the AI) from re-discovering the same site-specific failures.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Amazon's search results page returns empty product cards when using JS injection (document.querySelectorAll) immediately after navigation. Their bot detection flags programmatic fetch()/XHR calls and headless-looking query patterns, returning either blank results or a CAPTCHA page.

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text: Amazon detects query patterns from document.querySelectorAll fired too early or via injected scripts that look automated. They also check for suspiciously fast post-navigation execution. The page is an SPA that hydrates asynchronously, so selectors valid in DevTools may return nothing if queried before hydration.

docs.title: What Does NOT Work
docs.text:
{ "action": "js", "code": "document.querySelectorAll('[data-component-type=\"s-search-result\"]')" }
Fired immediately after navigate → returns [] even though the page looks loaded. Amazon may also serve a bot-check interstitial if requests look automated.

docs.title: Step 1 — Navigate with a human-style search URL (sorted, filtered)
docs.text:
{ "action": "navigate", "url": "https://www.amazon.com/s?k=gaming+desktop+pc&rh=p_36%3A-200000&s=review-rank" }
Use s=review-rank for best-rated first. Use rh=p_36%3A-200000 for under $2000.

docs.title: Step 2 — Scroll to trigger hydration
docs.text:
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "waitForElement", "selector": "[data-component-type='s-search-result']", "timeout": 12000 },
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 }
amount is in pixels; 800 is roughly one viewport height. Triggers hydration of lazy-loaded cards.

docs.title: Step 3 — Extract AFTER scrolling (products are now rendered)
docs.text:
{
  "action": "js",
  "code": "JSON.stringify([...document.querySelectorAll('[data-component-type=\"s-search-result\"]')].slice(0,10).map(el => ({ name: el.querySelector('h2 span')?.innerText?.trim(), price: el.querySelector('.a-price .a-offscreen')?.innerText?.trim(), rating: el.querySelector('.a-icon-alt')?.innerText?.trim() })).filter(x => x.name))"
}

docs.title: Key Selectors (verified 2026-03-12)
docs.text: Data Selector Product card container [data-component-type="s-search-result"] Product name h2 span (inside card) Price .a-price .a-offscreen Star rating .a-icon-alt

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Kitsune runs as a real browser extension in a real browser session — this is the core advantage. Amazon can't distinguish it from a normal user browsing.
  • Never use fetch() or XMLHttpRequest via js action to hit Amazon endpoints — those are fingerprinted. Only read the already-rendered DOM.
  • If results still empty, add a sleep of 1500ms before the JS extraction step.
  • The waitForElement on the product card selector is the reliable gate — don't extract until it returns found: true.
  • Works whether tab is active or not as long as waitForElement confirms load.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Best Buy's search/category pages lazy-load product cards via intersection observers. The .sku-item selector (visible in DevTools on a fully loaded page) returns empty when queried immediately after navigation or when the tab is not the active/focused tab. Even after waitForElement reports a match, the list may be skeleton placeholders rather than real product data.

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text:
Best Buy uses React with virtual/windowed rendering. Product cards only fully hydrate when they enter the viewport. Running the tab in the background (e.g. in a parallel batch sequence) means the intersection observers never fire — nothing scrolls into view because the tab has no visible viewport.

Additionally, .sku-item is not the real product container in 2026. The live selector is .product-list-item (confirmed March 2026).

docs.title: What Does NOT Work
docs.text: Do NOT use .sku-item — this was the old selector and returns 0 results as of 2026.

docs.title: Step 1 — Navigate to a search URL with filters baked in
docs.text: { "action": "navigate", "url": "https://www.bestbuy.com/site/searchpage.jsp?st=gaming+desktop+pc&intl=nosplash&price=PCE_0~PCE_200000&sort=BESTSELLING", "expectTitle": "gaming" }

docs.title: Step 2 — Scroll to trigger lazy loading, then wait for results
docs.text:
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 1500 },
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 1500 },
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 2000 }
amount is in pixels; 800 is roughly one viewport height. Each scroll triggers intersection observers to render the next batch of lazy-loaded product cards.

docs.title: Step 3 — Extract using correct 2026 selectors
docs.text:
{
  "action": "js",
  "code": "JSON.stringify([...document.querySelectorAll('.product-list-item')].slice(0,10).map(el => ({ name: el.querySelector('.product-title')?.innerText?.trim(), price: el.querySelector('[class*=price]')?.innerText?.trim()?.match(/\\$[\\d,\\.]+/)?.[0], rating: el.querySelector('[class*=rating]')?.getAttribute('aria-label') })).filter(x => x.name))"
}

docs.title: Key Selectors (verified 2026-03-12)
docs.text: Data Selector Product card container .product-list-item Product name .product-title Price [class*=price] → regex \$[\d,\.]+ Rating [class*=rating] → aria-label attribute

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Must be the active/focused tab for intersection observers to fire, OR use the scroll action (which triggers scrollBy internally and works in background tabs).
  • Parallel batch sequences may fail on Best Buy because background tabs don't always trigger lazy loading — run sequentially.
  • 500+ [class*=product] elements exist on the page — don't use that as a readiness check. Use .product-list-item count > 0 instead.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: B&H uses CSS Modules (hashed class names like product_UCJ1nUFwhh, listItem_tixYnI9pMn) that change with every frontend deploy. Selectors like [data-selenium="itemList"], .product, or .item return nothing because the actual class names are unguessable at write-time. Additionally, product cards lazy-load via intersection observers — same as Best Buy.

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text: B&H's frontend is built with CSS Modules where class names are generated at build time (e.g. product_UCJ1nUFwhh — a stable name + random hash). The hash portion changes on each deploy, making any hardcoded class name selector expire without warning. Standard semantic selectors (data-selenium, itemList, etc.) were present in older versions but appear removed in 2026.

docs.title: What Does NOT Work
docs.text:
{ "action": "waitForElement", "selector": "[data-selenium='itemList']", "timeout": 12000 }
Times out — attribute no longer exists on product cards in 2026.

{ "action": "js", "code": "document.querySelectorAll('[class*=product]')" }
Matches too broadly (nav items, wrappers, etc.) — not the product cards.

docs.title: What WORKS — Wildcard Selector + innerText Parsing
docs.text: The prefix before the underscore (product_) is stable across deploys even when the hash changes. Use [class*="product_"] as the selector.

docs.title: Step 1 — Parse innerText (more reliable than child selectors)
docs.text:
B&H product card innerText is structured and parseable. Use regex and string matching on el.innerText rather than child element selectors: 

const lines = el.innerText?.split('\n').filter(l => l.trim());
const name = lines?.find(l => l.match(/desktop|gaming|tower|pc/i)
  && !l.match(/compare|cart|stock|reviews|Promo|GHz|DDR|SSD|RTX|More|Save|Free|Add/i));
const priceMatch = el.innerText?.match(/\$(\d[\d,]+)\s*\n?\s*(\d{2})/);
const price = priceMatch ? `$${priceMatch[1]}.${priceMatch[2]}` : el.innerText?.match(/\$[\d,]+/)?.[0];
const rating = el.innerText?.match(/(\d+) Reviews/)?.[1];

docs.title: Full extraction sequence
docs.text:
{ "action": "navigate", "url": "https://www.bhphotovideo.com/c/search?Ntt=gaming+desktop+pc&MaxPrice=2000&SortOrder=CustomerRankDsc", "expectTitle": "gaming" },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 3000 },
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 1500 },
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 1500 },
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 1500 },
{ "action": "js", "code": "JSON.stringify([...document.querySelectorAll('[class*=\"product_\"]')].slice(0,10).map(el => { const lines = el.innerText?.split('\\n').filter(l => l.trim()); const name = lines?.find(l => l.match(/desktop|gaming|tower|pc/i) && !l.match(/compare|cart|stock|reviews|Promo|GHz|DDR|SSD|RTX|More|Save|Free|Add/i)); const priceMatch = el.innerText?.match(/\\$(\\d[\\d,]+)\\s*\\n?\\s*(\\d{2})/); const price = priceMatch ? ('$' + priceMatch[1] + '.' + priceMatch[2]) : el.innerText?.match(/\\$[\\d,]+/)?.[0]; const rating = el.innerText?.match(/(\\d+) Reviews/)?.[1]; return name ? {name: name.trim(), price, rating: rating ? rating + ' reviews' : null} : null }).filter(Boolean))" }

docs.title: Key Selectors (verified 2026-03-12)
docs.text: Data Selector / Method Product card container [class*="product_"] (wildcard prefix) Product name Parse innerText lines — filter for gaming keywords Price Regex \$(\d[\d,]+)\s*\n?\s*(\d{2}) on innerText Rating Regex (\d+) Reviews on innerText

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The [class*="prefix_"] wildcard pattern is the key insight — CSS Modules always use word_hash format, so the prefix before the underscore is stable across deploys. This works for B&H and any other CSS-Modules-based site.
  • If [class*="product_"] stops matching, re-sniff with the class discovery snippet in Step 1 to find the new prefix.
  • B&H lazy-loads but scroll with amount: 800 (pixels, roughly one viewport height) works reliably (same as Best Buy).
  • SortOrder=CustomerRankDsc sorts by customer rating descending — most useful for "best" queries.
  • Watch out for nav/filter [class*="item_"] elements — they look similar but their innerText will be short brand/category names, not product descriptions.

docs.title: Appendix: Debugging — Class Name Discovery
docs.text:
If [class*="product_"] stops matching after a B&H deploy, sniff the live class names to find the new prefix: 

{
  "action": "js",
  "code": "JSON.stringify([...new Set([...document.querySelectorAll('[class]')].flatMap(e => [...e.classList]).filter(c => c.match(/^(item|product|card|result)_[a-zA-Z0-9]+$/)))].slice(0,10))"
}
This returns all CSS Modules classes matching the word_hash pattern. Look for the one used on product card containers and update the wildcard selector above.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Search results (/sch/i.html) no longer match li.s-item, the selector most eBay scrapers and older answers use: it returns 0 items. Switching to the new card class looks right but returns 62 items on a 60-item page, and the card text carries noise that breaks naive parsing: screen-reader text in titles, badges glued onto titles, original prices glued onto current prices, and a reversed "Sponsored" label on every card.

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text:
• The results list is rendered with s-card / su-card-container components.
  • Two hidden "Shop on eBay" placeholder cards (1 px wide, $20.00) sit outside ul.srp-results but still have class="s-card" and a data-listingid.
  • ul.srp-results also holds non-card lis (a filter carousel and the pagination block).
  • Inside a card:
  • .s-card__title includes a hidden <span class="clipped">Opens in a new window or tab</span>.
  • New listings have a <span class="s-card__new-listing">NEW LISTING</span> before the title span inside .s-card__title; some cards have a .s-card__caption ("NEW LOW PRICE") above the title link.
  • Discounted items render the original price in a .strikethrough span in the same row as the current price, so the row text reads KRW56,429.79KRW66,392.66.
  • Every card checked (60/60) has derosnopS ("Sponsored" reversed) in its footer text; the visible "Sponsored" label is drawn from an SVG background image instead.
  • Prices are shown in a currency chosen for the visitor (KRW from Korea in testing), not by the ship-to country.

docs.title: What Does NOT Work
docs.text: Selector or approach Result li.s-item 0 matches li.s-card, [data-listingid] 62 on a 60-item page: includes the two placeholders ul.srp-results > li 62: includes the filter carousel and pagination lis .s-card__title text Ends with "Opens in a new window or tab" .s-card__title > span:first-child Returns NEW LISTING on new listings .s-card__subtitle 61 on 60 cards: one card repeated its condition row .s-card__subtitle-row:nth-of-type(1) > .s-card__subtitle 57: the "NEW LOW PRICE" caption shifts nth-of-type .s-card__price 104 spans: includes placeholders and the to of price ranges; cannot be aligned with cards Text search for "Sponsored" Never matches; derosnopS was on every card checked, so it cannot classify sponsored listings either _fcid=<country id> URL parameter Changes the session's ship-to country (it persists in later searches) and does not change the currency. Avoid it in the user's own browser; see Notes to restore it

docs.title: Step 1 — Build the search URL
docs.text: Parameter Effect (verified 2026-10-25) _nkw=mechanical+keyboard Keywords _ipg=120 Items per page (default 60); returned exactly 120 cards _pgn=2 Page number _sop=15 Sort shown as "Price + Shipping: lowest first" LH_BIN=1 Buy It Now only (all 120 cards showed "Buy It Now") LH_ItemCondition=1000 New (all 120 cards showed "Brand New")

docs.title: Step 2 — Extract with one selector per field
docs.text:
Each selector below matched exactly one element per card (60/60 and 120/120), so the result arrays line up by index. All text is already rendered after navigate, in a background tab, without scrolling.

[
  { "action": "navigate", "url": "https://www.ebay.com/sch/i.html?_nkw=mechanical+keyboard&LH_BIN=1&LH_ItemCondition=1000&_sop=15&_ipg=120&_pgn=1", "expectTitle": "Mechanical Keyboard" },
  { "action": "query", "selector": "h1.srp-controls__count-heading", "fields": ["text"], "limit": 1 },
  { "action": "query", "selector": "ul.srp-results > li.s-card", "fields": ["data-listingid"], "limit": 120 },
  { "action": "query", "selector": "ul.srp-results > li.s-card .s-card__title > span.su-styled-text", "fields": ["text"], "limit": 120 },
  { "action": "query", "selector": "ul.srp-results > li.s-card .su-card-container__attributes__primary > .s-card__attribute-row:first-child", "fields": ["text"], "limit": 120 },
  { "action": "query", "selector": "ul.srp-results > li.s-card .s-card__link + .s-card__subtitle-row > .s-card__subtitle", "fields": ["text"], "limit": 120 }
]

Run it with browser_batch (automation group). navigate is core and query is read, for example KITSUNE_CAPS=core,automation,read. Pass limit to cover the page size (browser_query defaults to 50). No step needs the developer build.

The item URL is https://www.ebay.com/itm/<data-listingid>. The card links are the same URL with tracking parameters.

docs.title: Step 3 — Parse the price row
docs.text:
The price row text takes four observed forms:

Row text Meaning KRW39,684.20 Single price KRW119,488.26 to KRW142,430.64 Variation listing: price range KRW56,429.79KRW66,392.66 Price, then the strikethrough original price KRW32,772.94 to KRW72,809.64KRW51,587.28 Range, then the original price 
PRICE = re.compile(r"(?:[A-Z]{1,3} ?)?[$£€]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
tokens = PRICE.findall(row)
if " to " in row:
    low, high, was = tokens[0], tokens[1], tokens[2] if len(tokens) > 2 else None
else:
    low = high = tokens[0]; was = tokens[1] if len(tokens) > 1 else None

Only KRW prices were observed; check the format before relying on this for other currencies.

Shipping, buying format and item location are later rows of the same block. Query ul.srp-results > li.s-card .su-card-container__attributes__primary with fields: ["text"] (also one per card) and split the lines: the first line is the price row, then rows such as Buy It Now, +KRW7,449.60 shipping or Free International Shipping, and from China. The rows that appear vary by listing, so match them by text, not position.

docs.title: Key Selectors (verified 2026-10-25, signed extension build, not signed in to eBay)
docs.text: Data Selector Result card (excludes placeholders and non-card rows) ul.srp-results > li.s-card Listing ID data-listingid attribute of the card Title .s-card__title > span.su-styled-text "NEW LISTING" badge .s-card__new-listing Price row .su-card-container__attributes__primary > .s-card__attribute-row:first-child Original (strikethrough) price .strikethrough inside the price row Condition .s-card__link + .s-card__subtitle-row > .s-card__subtitle Result count h1.srp-controls__count-heading (e.g. 12,000+ results for mechanical keyboard) Sort control button[aria-label^='Sort']

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Currency and ship-to: the header button button.gh-ship-to__menu and the results' "Shipping to:" flyout (button.x-flyout__button) show the ship-to location. To restore it after an accidental change, open the flyout, pick the country in its select (option values are eBay country IDs, e.g. 1 United States, 111 South Korea), and press its Go input. A previous postal code may not be restored.
  • Relevance: the default "Best Match" sort mixes in off-topic items and sponsored placements. Filter results yourself.
  • Sort order is not by the displayed price: _sop=15 sorts by price plus shipping, and variation listings show a range. Re-sort client-side if order matters.
  • Validate the page before parsing: compare the card count with the _ipg you asked for. A count that is 2 higher means the placeholders slipped into the selector.
  • The image selector .su-card-container__media li:first-child img.s-card__image matched 0 cards; images were not verified.
  • Item pages (/itm/…) were not covered by this playbook.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Newegg's SubCategory URLs (e.g. /gaming-pcs/SubCategory/ID-3319) with facet filter params (N=4131) silently redirect to completely unrelated categories. In testing, the gaming desktop category URL redirected to Correction Fluids & Erasers — the N= facet ID had been reassigned. The page title changes but the URL stays the same, making it non-obvious that you're on the wrong page.

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text: Newegg's facet/filter parameter N= is an internal numeric ID that gets recycled and reassigned across categories. Bookmarking or hardcoding these URLs breaks silently over time. The SubCategory/ID-XXXX segment is also unstable.

docs.title: What Does NOT Work
docs.text:
https://www.newegg.com/gaming-pcs/SubCategory/ID-3319?N=4131&Price=-200000
https://www.newegg.com/gaming-pcs/SubCategory/ID-3319?Price=-200000&Order=RATING
Both redirected to office supplies (Correction Fluids & Erasers) in March 2026. Always verify with document.title before trusting results — if the title doesn't match your category, you've been silently redirected.

Use expectTitle on navigate to catch redirects automatically — Kitsune will return a warning and redirected: true if the page title doesn't match.

docs.title: Stable search URL format
docs.text:
https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?d=gaming+desktop+rtx&Order=RATING&Price=-200000
- d= is the search query — use keywords, not category IDs - Order=RATING sorts by customer rating - Price=-200000 caps at $2000 (Newegg uses cents: 200000 = $2000)

docs.title: Full extraction sequence
docs.text:
{ "action": "navigate", "url": "https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?d=gaming+desktop+rtx&Order=RATING&Price=-200000", "expectTitle": "gaming" },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 3000 },
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 1500 },
{ "action": "scroll", "direction": "down", "amount": 800 },
{ "action": "sleep", "ms": 1500 },
{
  "action": "js",
  "code": "JSON.stringify([...document.querySelectorAll('.item-cell')].slice(0,10).map(el => ({ name: el.querySelector('.item-title')?.innerText?.trim(), price: '$' + el.querySelector('.price-current strong')?.innerText?.trim(), rating: el.querySelector('.item-rating-num')?.innerText?.trim() })).filter(x => x.name && x.price !== '$undefined'))"
}

docs.title: Key Selectors (verified 2026-03-12)
Notes
docs.text:
• Always validate document.title after navigation before extracting — silent redirects are Newegg's biggest gotcha.
  • The /p/pl?d= format is the most stable URL pattern — it's the same URL structure their own search bar uses, so it won't go stale.
  • Refurbished and used listings appear in results — filter by checking if the name contains "REFURBISHED" or "USED" if you want new-only.
  • N= facet params are ephemeral — never hardcode them.
  • .item-cell selector works reliably on the /p/pl results page.
